mainTopic: בל תחסום: threshing תרומה and מעשר, the reason behind the ban, and telling a נכרי to muzzle
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא: cows threshing תרומה or מעשר may be muzzled without breaking בל תחסום. For appearance's sake, though, the owner hangs food by the cow's mouth, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says כרשינים are best. A second ברייתא rules the opposite. The גמרא settles the תרומה clash with real תרומה versus גידולי תרומה. That answer fails for מעשר, so the גמרא offers several other answers: מעשר ראשון versus מעשר שני; a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about whether מעשר שני is מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ; and ודאי versus דמאי, which it finally reworks into תרומת מעשר, since there is no תרומת דמאי. Next, רב ששת uses רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's teaching to show that the ban on muzzling exists for the animal's benefit. The גמרא then asks whether a Jew may tell a נכרי to muzzle his cow. One proof is pushed aside, and a second proof, about a question sent to שמואל's father, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Cows threshing תרומה and מעשר may be muzzled, but hang food for appearance
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that muzzling cows that thresh תרומה or מעשר does not break בל תחסום. Because of מראית העין, though, the owner hangs some of that same produce by the cow's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And cows that thresh תרומה and מעשר: he does not break the rule of 'do not muzzle.' But because of how it looks, he brings a bundle of that same kind of produce and hangs it in the basket at her mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about when the rule of בל תחסום does not apply. Here the case is cows threshing holy produce (תרומה and מעשר).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cow is not allowed to eat תרומה or מעשר, so muzzling her here is not a violation. But people watching might think he is breaking בל תחסום. So he hangs ordinary food of the same kind by her mouth, so it looks like she is eating what she threshes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Do not muzzle': the Torah ban on muzzling an ox while it threshes
The portion of produce given to a כהן; others may not eat it
A tithe, a tenth of the produce that is set aside
How something looks to others; avoiding the look of doing something wrong
A basket hung by the animal's mouth

steps.confusionAlert: Hanging the food is not required by the Torah law of בל תחסום. That law does not apply here at all. It is only done so it does not look wrong.

phrases.english: And those that thresh תרומה and tithe,
phrases.notes: "Those" means cows. This finishes a ברייתא that started on the previous page.

phrases.english: he does not transgress 'Do not muzzle,'
but because of how it looks to others,
he brings a bundle of that same species
and hangs it for her in the basket that is at her mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַדָּשׁוֹת בִּתְרוּמָה וּמַעֲשֵׂר, אֵינוֹ עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל תַּחְסוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Muzzling cows that thresh תרומה or מעשר is not a violation of בל תחסום, but for appearance's sake one hangs produce of the same species by the cow's mouth.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: hang vetches instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says the owner may hang כרשינים, since they are the best food for the cow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says: He brings vetches and hangs them for her, because vetches are better for her than anything.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא says which food to hang by the cow's mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion wants the same kind of produce the cow is threshing. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says it does not have to match. כרשינים are fine because the cow likes them most.

keyTerms.meaning: Vetches, a kind of animal feed
A תנא who gives a second opinion here

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:
He brings vetches and hangs them for her,
because vetches are better for her than anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion on how to carry out the ruling in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may hang vetches rather than the same species, since vetches are the cow's best food.

steps.title: A second ברייתא says threshing תרומה and מעשר does involve בל תחסום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא that says threshing תרומה and מעשר DOES break בל תחסום. This contradicts the first ברייתא for both תרומה and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: Cows that tread on grain: he does not break 'do not muzzle.' Cows that thresh תרומה and מעשר: he does break 'do not muzzle.' A non-Jew threshing with a Jew's cow does not break it. A Jew threshing with a non-Jew's cow does break it. This is a difficulty, תרומה against תרומה, and מעשר against מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different ברייתא that rules the opposite about threshing תרומה and מעשר. It then states the problem plainly: the two sources clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said muzzling here is no violation. This ברייתא says it is a violation. Both seem to be about the same case, so the גמרא points out two clashes: one about תרומה and one about מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted it': a formula that brings a source contradicting the one before
Treading or trampling on the produce
A non-Jew
'It is difficult': a contradiction or problem

steps.confusionAlert: In the ownership cases, what matters is who does the threshing, not who owns the cow. A Jew threshing breaks the rule even with a non-Jew's cow.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: Cows that tread on grain,
he does not transgress 'Do not muzzle.'
And those that thresh תרומה and tithe,
he does transgress 'Do not muzzle.'
phrases.notes: This is the exact opposite of what the first ברייתא said in step 1.

phrases.english: And a non-Jew who threshes with a Jew's cow,
he does not transgress 'Do not muzzle.'
And a Jew who threshes with a non-Jew's cow,
he does transgress 'Do not muzzle.'
It is difficult: תרומה against תרומה,
it is difficult: tithe against tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 with a contradicting ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 1 that muzzling cows threshing תרומה and מעשר is not a violation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא explicitly rules that it IS a violation, in what looks like the same case.

steps.title: The תרומה clash is solved: real תרומה versus its growths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the תרומה contradiction. One ברייתא speaks about actual תרומה, and the other about גידולי תרומה, which are only תרומה מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, תרומה against תרומה is not a difficulty: here it is about real תרומה, and there it is about produce grown from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the first half of the problem, the clash about תרומה, by saying each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Real תרומה may not be fed to the cow, so muzzling her is fine (first ברייתא). גידולי תרומה are only תרומה by rabbinic law, so the cow may eat them, and muzzling her breaks בל תחסום (second ברייתא).

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted': this part works fine (it sets up a 'but' that is coming next)
'Here... there': splitting two sources into two different cases
Produce grown from planted תרומה seeds

phrases.english: Granted, תרומה against תרומה is not difficult:
here it is about תרומה itself,
there it is about the growths of תרומה.
phrases.notes: "Growths" means a new crop that grew from planted תרומה seeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers half of the contradiction raised in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different type of produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be about the same תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: First ברייתא: actual תרומה. Second ברייתא: גידולי תרומה.

steps.title: But the מעשר clash still stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the contradiction about מעשר is still a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: But tithe against tithe is still a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: Right after solving the תרומה clash, the גמרא says the מעשר clash is still unsolved. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be tried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'granted' in step 4 already hinted at this: one problem is solved, but the other remains. The rest of the section checks whether the same answer can work for מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But': it turns to the part that still does not work

phrases.english: But tithe against tithe is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the remaining problem after step 4's partial answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות' rulings on מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer given for תרומה has not yet been shown to work for מעשר, so the clash remains.

steps.title: A suggested answer: real מעשר versus its growths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests using the same answer for מעשר: one ברייתא is about real מעשר, the other about גידולי מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say tithe against tithe is also not a difficulty: here it is about real tithe, there about produce grown from tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for מעשר using the same split that worked for תרומה. The words 'if you would say' signal that this answer is about to be rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is the same as before: real מעשר cannot be fed to the cow, but its growths could be. That would explain why the two ברייתות rule differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you would say': brings a suggestion that will soon be pushed away
Also
Produce grown from planted מעשר seeds

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַעֲשֵׂר אַמַּעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: And if you would say tithe against tithe is also not difficult:
here, it is about tithe itself,
there, it is about the growths of tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַעֲשֵׂר אַמַּעֲשֵׂר נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to apply step 4's answer to the problem in step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposed case-split, copied from the תרומה answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps גידולי מעשר are like גידולי תרומה
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: first ברייתא is about actual מעשר, second about גידולי מעשר (rejected in step 7)

steps.title: Rejected: growths of מעשר are ordinary food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. גידולי תרומה still count as תרומה, but גידולי מעשר are plain חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, growths of תרומה are תרומה. But growths of tithe are ordinary, non-holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the answer from step 6 fails. The comparison between תרומה and מעשר does not hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split worked for תרומה because its growths still have some holiness. גידולי מעשר have no holiness at all. So a ברייתא could never call them 'מעשר', and the split cannot explain the clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food
'They are'

phrases.english: Granted, growths of תרומה are תרומה!
But growths of tithe are non-holy food.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא גִּידּוּלֵי תְרוּמָה תְּרוּמָה אֶלָּא גִּידּוּלֵי מַעֲשֵׂר חוּלִּין נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer proposed in step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proposed answer for the מעשר contradiction
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes גידולי מעשר keep the status of מעשר, but they are חולין

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: growths of טבל and מעשר שני are חולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves its point from a משנה that says גידולי טבל and גידולי מעשר שני are חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Growths of untithed produce and growths of second tithe are ordinary, non-holy food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its rejection with a clear source. Since growths of מעשר are חולין, this answer fails, and the next step gives a new answer for the מעשר contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says outright that produce grown from מעשר שני is not holy. This confirms step 7. The suggested split in step 6 cannot work, so the גמרא needs a different answer for the מעשר clash, which the next step gives.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As we learned in a משנה': brings a משנה as proof
Produce from which תרומה and מעשר have not yet been taken
Second tithe, eaten in ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: The תרומה contradiction is solved: real תרומה versus גידולי תרומה. The same answer fails for מעשר, because a משנה teaches that גידולי מעשר are חולין. The next step gives a new answer for מעשר.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: Growths of untithed produce
and growths of second tithe are non-holy food!

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן גִּידּוּלֵי טֶבֶל וְגִידּוּלֵי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rejection in step 7
steps.raayaObject: The claim that גידולי מעשר are חולין
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות 9:4: גידולי טבל וגידולי מעשר שני חולין

steps.title: A new answer: first tithe versus second tithe
steps.stepSummary: Since the גידולי מעשר answer failed, the גמרא answers that one ברייתא is talking about מעשר ראשון and the other about מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not a contradiction: this ברייתא is about first tithe, and that ברייתא is about second tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fresh way to settle the contradiction between the two ברייתות about letting the animal eat מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות are not talking about the same kind of tithe. מעשר ראשון is given to a לוי and is treated like ordinary property, so the animal may eat it. מעשר שני has holiness and must be eaten in ירושלים, so the animal may not eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (signals a new answer that replaces the rejected one)
It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
First tithe, given to the לוי
Second tithe, which the owner eats in ירושלים

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
this one is about first tithe,
that one is about second tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from Step 6 (rejected in Steps 7-8) with a new distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: the two ברייתות speak about different kinds of מעשר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to discuss the same מעשר and to give opposite rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ruling is about מעשר ראשון and the other is about מעשר שני, so they do not clash.

steps.title: A second answer: both are about second tithe, but they follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, both ברייתות discuss מעשר שני, and the contradiction is a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: both are about second tithe, and it is not a contradiction. This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, and that one follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another way to answer the same contradiction. This time it says the two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of splitting the cases, this answer keeps the case the same (מעשר שני) and splits the opinions. The next step will explain what each תנא holds.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say (introduces another possible answer)
This one and that one: both
A תנא, a student of רבי עקיבא
A תנא, a colleague of רבי מאיר

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
this one and that one are both about second tithe,
and it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: this one follows Rabbi Meir, that one follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא וְהָא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the same contradiction answered in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different opinions: the ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to be speaking about the same מעשר שני with opposite rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: They really disagree. One follows רבי מאיר and the other follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Explaining the מחלוקת: whose money is second tithe?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני belongs to Heaven, so the animal may not eat it. רבי יהודה holds that it belongs to the owner, so the animal may eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ברייתא follows רבי מאיר, who says tithe is Heaven's property. That ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, who says second tithe is ordinary private property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind the second answer by showing what רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מעשר שני belongs to Heaven, the owner only has permission to eat it himself, so he cannot let his animal eat it. If it is the owner's own property, he may let his animal eat from it while it threshes.

keyTerms.meaning: Property of the Most High (belonging to Heaven)
Ordinary private property belonging to a person

steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether מעשר שני is מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ or מָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט comes up in many places in ש״ס, for example in buying and selling it or using it for קידושין.

phrases.english: This one follows Rabbi Meir, who says:
tithe is property of the Most High,
phrases.notes: He means מעשר שני here. The owner may eat it, but it doesn't truly belong to him.

phrases.english: that one follows Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
second tithe is ordinary private property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, דְּאָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂר מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the opinions behind the answer given in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ and the animal may not eat it. According to רבי יהודה, it is מָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט and the animal may eat it.

steps.title: How could tithes be under a threshing animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case looks like, since tithes are normally separated only after threshing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how this case could ever happen. The animal is still threshing, but tithes are usually taken only after the grain is threshed and piled up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות assume there is already מעשר lying under the animal while it threshes. That seems impossible, so the גמרא wants to know the real-life case.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does the case look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
phrases.notes: The question: how can grain being threshed already be מעשר, when tithes are taken only after threshing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical case behind the ברייתות discussed in Steps 9-11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How there could be מעשר under a threshing animal, when tithes are normally separated after threshing

steps.title: He separated the tithe early, while it was still on the stalks
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the owner separated מעשר early, while the grain was still on the stalks, before threshing.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he separated it early, while it was still on the stalks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the owner separated his מעשר early, before threshing, so the animal is now threshing grain that is already מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually tithes are separated at the end, after the grain is piled up. Here the owner did it ahead of time, which is why there is already מעשר for the animal to thresh.

keyTerms.meaning: He separated it early, ahead of the usual time
Stalks or ears of grain, before threshing

phrases.english: For example, where he separated it early, while still on the stalks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner separated the מעשר early, while the grain was still on the stalks, so it is already מעשר during threshing.

steps.title: But second tithe must be eaten inside the walls
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, how can the animal eat מעשר שני out in the field? מעשר שני must be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה? But it requires the wall!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second answer. Even if מעשר שני is the owner's property, it may only be eaten inside ירושלים, so how could the animal eat it while threshing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ownership is not the only issue. מעשר שני also has a place rule: it must be eaten within the city walls. A threshing floor is normally outside the city, so רבי יהודה's ruling seems impossible to carry out.

keyTerms.meaning: But it requires (introduces a challenge)
Wall, here meaning the city walls of ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה's view that מעשר שני is the owner's property does not cancel its holiness. It still must be eaten inside ירושלים. That is exactly what this question is pointing out.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Yehuda?
But it requires the wall!
phrases.notes: מעשר שני may only be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבי יהודה side of the answer from Steps 10-11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא allowing the animal to eat follows רבי יהודה and is about מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if מעשר שני is private property, it may only be eaten inside ירושלים, so an animal could not eat it on a threshing floor.

steps.title: He threshed inside the wall of בית פאגי
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the threshing took place inside the wall of בית פאגי, an outer part of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, where he threshed inside the wall of בית פאגי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the threshing happened inside the outer wall of ירושלים called בית פאגי, so the place rule is kept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The threshing floor was within the area that counts as inside the walls. So the animal is eating מעשר שני in the proper place, and רבי יהודה's ruling works. This ends the question, and the רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshed
An outer area of ירושלים, enclosed by its own wall

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for מעשר. (1) One ברייתא is about מעשר ראשון and the other about מעשר שני. (2) Both are about מעשר שני, and they follow רבי מאיר (מָמוֹן גָּבוֹהַּ, so the animal may not eat it) and רבי יהודה (מָמוֹן הֶדְיוֹט, so it may). The case is where the מעשר was separated early on the stalks, and the threshing was inside the wall of בית פאגי.

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁדָּשׁ לִפְנִים מֵחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי.
phrases.english: For example, where he threshed inside the wall of Beit Pagei.
phrases.notes: בית פאגי was an outer part of ירושלים with its own wall, so threshing there counts as inside the walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁדָּשׁ לִפְנִים מֵחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal seemed to be eating מעשר שני outside ירושלים, which is not allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The threshing was inside the wall of בית פאגי, which counts as inside the walls, so eating there is allowed.

steps.title: Another answer: definite tithe versus doubtful tithe
steps.stepSummary: Instead of a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the two ברייתות can be read as speaking about two different kinds of מעשר: ודאי and דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, you can answer differently: there is no contradiction. One ברייתא is talking about produce that definitely must be tithed, and the other is talking about דמאי, produce that we are only unsure about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new, different answer to the contradiction between the two ברייתות about whether the animal may eat מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last answer said the two ברייתות follow two different תנאים. Now the גמרא says both ברייתות can agree, because they speak about different cases. Real מעשר (ודאי) is stricter, so the animal may not eat it, while מעשר from דמאי is only a rabbinic rule and is more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: introduces a second, different answer
Tithe from produce that definitely was not tithed (a Torah obligation)
Produce bought from an עם הארץ, who might not have tithed it; חכמים required tithing it to be safe
Here... there: each source is talking about a different case

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a rejection of the first answer about רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. It is simply another way to solve the same contradiction.

phrases.english: If you wish, say: it is not difficult.
Here, it is about definite tithe;
there, it is about tithe of דמאי.
phrases.notes: דמאי is produce from someone we don't trust to have tithed, so it's tithed just in case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another independent answer to the original מעשר contradiction from steps 3 and 5. It is an alternative to both the ראשון/שני answer (step 9) and the תנאים answer (steps 10-15).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the two sources speak about different kinds of produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings about the same מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות can agree. One is about real מעשר, and the other is about מעשר of דמאי.

steps.title: Using the same answer for the תרומה contradiction
steps.stepSummary: Since we now split between ודאי and דמאי, the גמרא uses the same split to solve the contradiction about תרומה too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this answer, the contradiction between the two rulings about תרומה is also not a problem. One is about definite תרומה, and the other is about תרומה of דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the new answer from the last step and uses it on the second contradiction, the one about תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות also seemed to contradict each other about תרומה. The same idea works here: real תרומה is strict, but תרומה from דמאי would be more lenient. This step sets up the next question, which asks whether תרומת דמאי even exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this: carrying an answer over to a new case
The portion of produce given to a כהן
תרומה taken from produce of doubtful status

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
תרומה against תרומה is also not difficult:
here, it is about definite תרומה;
there, it is about תרומה of דמאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ודאי/דמאי split from step 16 to the תרומה contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Using the same case split for a second contradiction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rulings about תרומה contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: One ruling is about definite תרומה, and the other is about תרומת דמאי.

steps.title: There is no such thing as תרומת דמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this: חכמים never required separating תרומה from דמאי, because everyone already separated תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that there is מעשר of דמאי. But is there really תרומה of דמאי? A ברייתא teaches: יוחנן כהן גדול also stopped the declaration of tithes and made the rule about דמאי, because he sent messengers through all of ארץ ישראל and saw that people separated only תרומה גדולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from the last step by proving from a ברייתא that תרומת דמאי does not exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוחנן כהן גדול made the rule of דמאי because people were careless with מעשרות. But his messengers found that everyone did separate תרומה גדולה. So produce from an עם הארץ is never in doubt about תרומה, and there is no תרומת דמאי for the ברייתא to be talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense for X... but for Y? The typical way of setting up a challenge
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? A source brought to challenge
The declaration a farmer makes that he gave all his tithes
Made a rabbinic decree
The main תרומה, the first portion separated for the כהן

phrases.english: Granted, there is such a thing as tithe of דמאי;
but is there such a thing as תרומה of דמאי?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
He also canceled the declaration of tithes
phrases.notes: "He" is יוחנן כהן גדול. The declaration is from דברים 26:13.

phrases.english: and made a decree about דמאי,
because he sent messengers throughout all the borders of ישראל
and saw that they would not separate anything
except תרומה גדולה alone!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא מַעֲשֵׂר דְּמַאי אִיכָּא, אֶלָּא תְּרוּמַת דְּמַאי מִי אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17's claim that one ברייתא is talking about תרומת דמאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 17 that one ברייתא speaks about תרומת דמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone separated תרומה גדולה, so חכמים never required it from דמאי. That makes 'תרומת דמאי' a case that does not exist.

steps.title: The answer is about תרומת מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the answer: the split is between definite תרומת מעשר and תרומת מעשר of דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is not difficult: one ruling is about definite תרומת מעשר, and the other is about תרומת מעשר of דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by changing which kind of תרומה the ברייתות are talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה גדולה is never taken from דמאי. But תרומת מעשר, the portion the לוי gives the כהן from his מעשר, is taken from דמאי, since people were not careful about מעשר. So the split between ודאי and דמאי still works, as long as we read it as תרומת מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: drops the earlier answer for a better one
The tenth of his מעשר that a לוי gives to a כהן

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות agree. Real מעשר and real תרומת מעשר are strict, while those from דמאי are more lenient. There is no תרומת דמאי, because everyone separated תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: Rather, it is not difficult:
here, it is about definite תרומת מעשר;
there, it is about תרומת מעשר of דמאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 18 by changing תרומה to תרומת מעשר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the case split (a revised אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The split was between definite תרומה and תרומת דמאי, which does not exist.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split is between definite תרומת מעשר and תרומת מעשר of דמאי, which does exist.

steps.title: Question to רב ששת: an animal that eats and gets sick
steps.stepSummary: They ask רב ששת: if the threshing animal eats and gets diarrhea, may we muzzle it? It depends on the reason behind the מצוה of not muzzling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: if the animal was eating and getting diarrhea, what is the law? Is the reason we let it eat because the food is good for it, and this food is not good for it? Or is the reason that it sees food and suffers, and this animal also sees food and suffers?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The חכמים bring a question to רב ששת and lay out the two sides of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on why the Torah forbids muzzling. If the reason is to feed the animal, then food that makes it sick need not be allowed, and we may muzzle. If the reason is that seeing food it can't eat hurts the animal, this animal still feels that pain, so we may not muzzle.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked him: opens a question asked of a חכם
Has diarrhea
What is the law?
Or perhaps: brings the other side of a question
Suffers, is pained

steps.whyThisMatters: The question forces us to decide the reason behind לא תחסום: is it the animal's food, or the animal's pain?

phrases.english: They asked רב ששת:
If it was eating and getting diarrhea, what is the law?
Is it because the food is good for it,
and this food is not good for it?
Or perhaps it is because it sees the food and suffers,
and this one also sees the food and suffers?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה/מעשר discussion and starts a new question about the reason for not muzzling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May you muzzle a threshing animal when the food makes it sick? This depends on whether the reason for the מצוה is feeding the animal or sparing it pain.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחי about vetches
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says one may bring vetches and hang them for the cow, because vetches are best for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to them: You already learned the answer. רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: One may bring vetches and hang them for the cow, because vetches are better for it than anything else.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from step 20 by quoting a teaching of רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether we may muzzle an animal when its food makes it sick. רבי שמעון בן יוחי lets the owner give the cow a different food that is better for it. That shows the law cares about what is good for the animal, not just about letting it eat whatever is in front of it.

keyTerms.meaning: You already learned it (in a ברייתא)
Vetches, a plant used as animal feed
Hangs it for the animal, so it can eat from it

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to them: You learned it
Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
One brings vetches and hangs them for it,
for vetches are better for it than anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question put to רב ששת in step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יוחי lets one give the animal vetches, which are best for it. This shows the מצוה is about the animal's benefit.

steps.title: The reason is the animal's benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the reason for not muzzling is that eating is good for the animal, and it confirms this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that the reason is because the food is good for the animal. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from רבי שמעון בן יוחי and confirms it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the rule is about what is good for the animal, food that harms the animal is not protected by it. So when the food gives the animal diarrhea, we may stop it from eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; also used to confirm a conclusion
That it is good for it

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on muzzling is there for the animal's good. Food that harms the animal does not have to be allowed.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִשּׁוּם דִּמְעַלֵּי לַהּ הוּא.
phrases.english: Learn from this that it is because it is good for it.
Learn from it.
phrases.notes: Said a second time, it means the גמרא agrees: yes, that is the conclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מִשּׁוּם דִּמְעַלֵּי לַהּ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in step 21
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The reason for not muzzling is the animal's benefit. So an animal whose food harms it may be muzzled.

steps.title: May one tell a non-Jew to muzzle one's cow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether telling a נכרי to muzzle one's cow and thresh is forbidden. It asks whether the rabbinic ban on telling a נכרי applies only to שבת or to every prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: may a person say to a non-Jew, "Muzzle my cow and thresh with it"? Do we say that the rabbinic ban on telling a non-Jew applies only to שבת, whose violation carries stoning, and not to muzzling, which is a regular prohibition? Or perhaps there is no difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: may a Jew ask a נכרי to do the muzzling for him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know that telling a נכרי to do מלאכה on שבת is forbidden as a שבות. The question is whether the רבנן made this ban only for שבת, which is very severe and punished with סקילה, or also for an ordinary לאו like muzzling.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before the Sages
Telling a non-Jew to do something for you
A rabbinic prohibition
Stoning, the punishment for breaking שבת
An ordinary Torah prohibition

phrases.english: A question was asked:
What is the law if a person says to a non-Jew:
"Muzzle my cow and thresh with it"?
Do we say:
when we say that telling a non-Jew is a rabbinic prohibition,
that applies only to Shabbat
which is a prohibition punished by stoning,
but muzzling, which is a regular prohibition, no,
or perhaps there is no difference?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: מַהוּ שֶׁיֹּאמַר אָדָם לְנׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about muzzling, now about using a נכרי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the rabbinic ban on telling a נכרי to do a forbidden act applies only to שבת or to ordinary prohibitions like muzzling too

steps.title: Proof from a non-Jew threshing with a Jew's cow
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a נכרי threshing with a Jew's cow does not violate בל תחסום. The wording suggests that a lesser prohibition still exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A non-Jew who threshes with a Jew's cow does not violate "do not muzzle." This implies that it is only a Torah violation that is missing, but there is still a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from a ברייתא about a נכרי threshing with a Jew's muzzled cow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says only that there is no Torah violation. The גמרא reads this to mean that some rabbinic prohibition is still there. That would show that using a נכרי for muzzling is forbidden, just as it is on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; it introduces a proof
The Torah ban on muzzling a threshing animal
It is only a real violation that he does not commit

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A non-Jew who threshes with a Jew's cow
does not violate "do not muzzle."
It is a Torah violation that he does not commit,
but there is a prohibition.
phrases.notes: He means a smaller, rabbinic prohibition still applies here.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נׇכְרִי הַדָּשׁ בְּפָרָתוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a proof to answer the question of step 23
steps.raayaObject: That using a נכרי to muzzle is still forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא says the נכרי does not violate the Torah ban, which suggests a rabbinic ban remains

steps.title: The wording only matches the second half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. In truth there may be no prohibition at all, and the ברייתא said "does not violate" only to match its second half.
steps.simpleTranslation: By right, there is no prohibition either. But since the latter part taught that a Jew who threshes with a non-Jew's cow does violate, the first part was worded to match: "does not violate."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the proof by explaining why the ברייתא used that wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the ברייתא says a Jew threshing with a נכרי's cow "violates." So the first half was worded the opposite way, "does not violate," just to match. Because of that, we cannot learn from the wording that some prohibition remains.

keyTerms.meaning: By right; in truth
Since; because of
The latter part of a teaching
The first part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: "Does not violate" here does not prove a rabbinic ban exists. The wording was chosen only so the first half would match the second half.

phrases.english: By right, there is no prohibition either,
but since it taught in the latter part

phrases.aramaic: דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַדָּשׁ בְּפָרָתוֹ שֶׁל נׇכְרִי עוֹבֵר,
phrases.english: that a Jew who threshes with a non-Jew's cow violates,
it taught in the first part: "does not violate."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference from the wording "does not violate"
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording was chosen only to match the second half ("violates"), so it does not show that a rabbinic prohibition remains

steps.title: A question sent to שמואל's father about oxen
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second proof: a question about some oxen that was sent to the father of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: they sent a question to שמואל's father: These oxen...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new attempt to answer the question. It starts quoting a question about oxen sent to the father of שמואל, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first proof was pushed aside, so the גמרא looks for another source. The details of the case and how it helps will come in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent to him (a question in writing)
The father of שמואל
Oxen

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דִּשְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ לַאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for they sent to Shmuel's father:
These oxen

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דִּשְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ לַאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected in step 25, a new proof begins
steps.raayaObject: The question of step 23, whether one may tell a נכרי to muzzle
steps.raayaSupportSource: A question sent to the father of שמואל about oxen (it continues in the following text)
